# Warm CO Gas Generated by Possible Turbulent Shocks in a Low-mass Star-forming Dense Core in Taurus

`2018ApJ...862....8T` | The Astrophysical Journal 2018 | first author: Tokuda, Kazuki | arXiv: 1804.05603 | DOI: 10.3847/1538-4357/aac898

Card schema 1.0 | model claude-sonnet-5-5 | depth full | type observational_alma_primary

## Science

- Fields: star_formation, milky_way_ism
- Question: What is the origin of warm CO gas structures in the cold dense core MC27/L1521F, and can they be explained by turbulent shocks?  
  > "We suggest that the warm CO clouds may be consequences of shock heating induced by interactions among the different density/velocity components that originated from the turbulent motions in the core." (abstract)
- Target **MC27/L1521F**: coordinates RA 4h28m38.996s, Dec +26d51m35.0s (J2000)  
  > "toward MC27/L1521F with a center position of ($\alpha_{J2000.0}$, $\delta_{J2000.0}$) = (4$^{\rm h}$28$^{\rm m}$38.996s, +26$^\circ$51$''$35.0$''$)" (2 Observations); "at a distance of the Taurus molecular cloud ($\sim$140 pc, (cite: Elias78))" (3.1 CO filaments); z/distance ~140 pc  
  > "toward MC27/L1521F with a center position of ($\alpha_{J2000.0}$, $\delta_{J2000.0}$) = (4$^{\rm h}$28$^{\rm m}$38.996s, +26$^\circ$51$''$35.0$''$)" (2 Observations); "at a distance of the Taurus molecular cloud ($\sim$140 pc, (cite: Elias78))" (3.1 CO filaments); distance from Elias78 (Taurus distance)  
  > "toward MC27/L1521F with a center position of ($\alpha_{J2000.0}$, $\delta_{J2000.0}$) = (4$^{\rm h}$28$^{\rm m}$38.996s, +26$^\circ$51$''$35.0$''$)" (2 Observations); "at a distance of the Taurus molecular cloud ($\sim$140 pc, (cite: Elias78))" (3.1 CO filaments)

## Analysis recipe

1. **Image and combine datasets**: Reduce in CASA, taper 12 m data, feather 12 m + 7 m + TP  
  > "We combined the datasets (12 m + 7 m + TP) by using the feathering technique" (2 Observations)
   - software: CASA
   - parameter: briggs robust 0.5 before tapering  
  > "by using the briggs weighting with the robust parameter of 0.5" (2 Observations)
   - fitting: _not stated_
   - validation: 1.3 mm continuum compared with earlier images  
  > "the 1.3 mm continuum observations reproduce the previously obtained continuum images well" (2 Observations)
2. **Estimate optical depth, column density and temperature of Bright filament**: 12CO(3-2)/13CO(2-1) peak intensity ratio with opacity equation, 13CO column density  
  > "We thus estimate the optical depth of $^{12}$CO, $\tau_{12}$, from the intensity ratio of $^{12}$CO ($J$= 3–2) and $^{13}$CO ($J$= 2–1)" (3.1 CO filaments)
   - parameter: 12CO smoothed to ~0.5"; peak ~50 K  
  > "the peak brightness temperature of the Bright filament is measured as $\sim$50 K" (3.1 CO filaments)
   - assumption: 12CO(3-2) optically thick; 12CO/13CO ~70; 13CO/H2 = 1.4e-6  
  > "We assume that $^{12}$CO ($J$= 3–2) is optically thick and that the peak temperature is the same as that of $^{12}$CO ($J$= 2–1)." (3.1 CO filaments)
   - fitting: _not stated_
   - validation: tau consistent with earlier study  
  > "This value is also consistent with that derived from the earlier study (cite: Takahashi13)." (3.1 CO filaments)
3. **Identify tiny CO clumps**: Dendrogram leaves with peak Tb between 15 and 35 K  
  > "the maximum and minimum peak brightness temperature at the leaves are 15 and 35 K" (3.2 Tiny CO clumps)
   - software: astrodendro
   - assumption: N from X_CO = 2e20 with CO(3-2)/(1-0) ratio of 1  
  > "with an assumption of CO ($J$ = 3–2)/CO ($J$ = 1–0) intensity ratio of 1" (Appendix)
   - fitting: _not stated_
   - validation: _not stated_
4. **Mass/column of arc-like structure and velocity components**: LTE optically thin 13CO with 12 m data alone; centroid velocities of components  
  > "Under the assumption of the LTE condition and optically thin emission, we estimate the mass and column density from the $^{13}$CO observations" (3.3 13CO and C18O)
   - fitting: Single Gaussian fits for line widths  
  > "by fitting the profile with a single Gaussian profile" (Table 2)
   - validation: _not stated_
5. **Test shock heating**: 1D Rankine-Hugoniot shock model, compare with observed temperature  
  > "the maximum temperature at the shock front becomes $\sim$200 K in the case of the downstream velocity of 2 km s$^{-1}$" (4.1 Possible origins)
   - parameter: preshock 1e5 cm^-3, 10 K  
  > "We set the gas density of 10$^5$ cm$^{-3}$ and the temperature of 10 K at the preshock layer" (4.1 Possible origins)
   - assumption: dust cooling only; no molecular line cooling  
  > "Because the main coolants are dust particles, molecular line cooling is not considered in the simulation." (4.1 Possible origins)
   - fitting: _not stated_
   - validation: consistent with ~60 K of Bright filament at ~300 au  
  > "The temperature at a distance of $\sim$300 au from the shock front is $\sim$60 K." (4.1 Possible origins)

## Qualitative findings

- High-density parts (protostar, MMS-2, MMS-3) are slightly redshifted from the core systemic velocity of 6.5 km/s  
  > "the central velocities of MMS-1, -2 and -3 are slightly redshifted from that of the parental core, 6.5 km s$^{-1}$" (3.3 13CO and C18O)

## Claim tuples

- H: Is the warm CO gas heated by the protostar? | E: Radiative-equilibrium temperature profile with protostar T at 1 au = 180 K | R: Only out to ~10 au can reach 60 K | F: Protostellar heating is unlikely | **supported**
- H: Can turbulent shocks produce the warm CO gas? | E: 1D shock model plus velocity-component maps | R: ~60 K at ~300 au from shock front; complementary blue/red clouds | F: Shock heating by interacting velocity components is a plausible origin | **partially**
- H: Is the turbulence consistent with Larson's law? | E: Compare required velocity with Larson relation | R: Larson's law gives <0.1 km/s at <1e3 au | F: Not a simple extension of Larson's law; origin unresolved | **supported**

## Reasoning

- Why this data: _not stated_
- Why this method: _not stated_
- Alternative: Protostellar heating rejected; past outflow not excluded  
  > "There is no strong evidence to exclude the third possibility as well." (4.1 Possible origins)
- How they decided it was enough: _not stated_
- Limitation (authors): 12CO cannot trace total gas mass due to self-absorption; large missing flux in 13CO/C18O  
  > "The $^{12}$CO observations, therefore, cannot trace the total gas mass at the line of sight due to the self-absorption" (3.1 CO filaments)
- Caveat (inferred, ours): Shock model is simple 1D with few parameters; no line-cooling
- Caveat (inferred, ours): Temperature assumes optically thick 12CO at peak with beam dilution
- Caveat (inferred, ours): Dendrogram parameters unspecified
- Caveat (inferred, ours): External vs internal turbulence origin undetermined
